metaTitle: Sliding Glass Door Repair Hialeah | Older Doors and Parts
description: Most Hialeah homes predate 1990. What sliding glass door repair in Hialeah looks like on an old slider: finding the maker, parts and the 1994 code date.
h1: Sliding glass door repair in Hialeah
subline: More than three quarters of Hialeah's homes were built before 1990, so the first question about a failing slider is how old it is.
answer: Sliding glass door repair in Hialeah often means an older slider. Start by finding the maker's label and measuring the rollers and handle, because parts for discontinued doors can be hard to find. Inland, heat and sun wear plastic parts more than salt does. If the door is finished, Hialeah's building department handles the replacement permit.
faqHeading: Questions about older doors in Hialeah
closing: Send a photo of the bottom corner of the panel and any label on the glass. We'll tell you whether the parts still exist before anyone comes out.

faqs.q: How do I find out who made my old sliding door?
faqs.a: Look for a name etched into a corner of the glass or a label on the edge of the frame. With a brand and model, the parts search is quick. Without one, the door gets identified by measuring the roller, the handle's screw spacing and the panel, not by matching looks.

faqs.q: Does the 25% rule apply to my Hialeah house?
faqs.a: It may, if your home is a one- or two-family house built under codes in force before September 1, 1994. In the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone, those homes can replace up to 25% of their glass area within 12 months without impact protection. Hialeah's building department makes the call.

faqs.q: Who issues door replacement permits in Hialeah?
faqs.a: The City of Hialeah's own building department, not Miami-Dade County. Because Hialeah is in the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone, the new door needs an approval for HVHZ use, usually a Miami-Dade NOA. Ask the department what it needs before the door is ordered.

faqs.q: Do sliding doors last longer inland than near the beach?
faqs.a: Inland doors generally need less frequent maintenance, in our founder's experience, because salt is what speeds up corrosion on rollers and tracks. Heat and sun still take a toll. Plastic wheels, guides and handle pieces break down over the years, especially on a west-facing slider.

faqs.q: Are nylon rollers OK for a house away from the coast?
faqs.a: Usually, yes. Away from salt water, a good nylon or steel roller is normally fine, and stainless mostly earns its higher price near the coast. Whatever the material, match the new roller to the old one by measurement, because two rollers that look alike can differ in the housing or wheel.
